executive_summary: SGD/CHF closed at 0.64923 on 2026-10-05 in the gated price store. The pair is quoted in Swiss francs per Singapore dollar, so a rising pair means a stronger Singapore dollar. It is up 1.54% over one month, 3.90% over three months, 4.79% over six months and 5.96% over a year, and sits at the 90th percentile of its 52-week close range (0.60555-0.65408). The pair cleanly expresses a split in policy regimes. MAS runs an appreciating S$NEER band at about 1.25% a year with a tightening bias and core inflation at 2.2%. The SNB sits at 0.00% with core at 0.4-0.5% and a three-year conditional forecast built on no change. On the 6-month T-bill proxy that gives the long-SGD leg about 192bp of carry, making this the only major Singapore dollar cross on which SGD earns carry rather than paying it. The bilateral view differs from both dossiers. The dollar headwind that holds the SGD dossier at Neutral tactically does not apply here, and the franc's place as the weakest currency in its own cross-section (11th of 11 tactically) sits directly against the Singapore dollar's third-place tactical ranking. The settled direction verdict is Bullish on both horizons at conviction 3 (tactical net +0.278, strategic +0.3938), and this report builds levels around it: a tactical base case retest of 0.6550 within four weeks, a strategic base case of 0.6640 by end-Q1 2027, entries preferred on dips into 0.6466-0.6480, and a daily-close stop below 0.6375. Structurally, spot is sitting on its 200-week average (0.64853, falling about 3 pips a week) inside a five-touch zone at 0.64661-0.65065. It was rejected on 1 October from a 52-week intraday high of 0.65500 in a key-reversal session, and the pair has not closed a week above that average in 123 weeks. The caveat is material and we state it plainly. Since pass 1 scored, French sovereign stress has escalated sharply: the OAT/Bund spread stood at 130.3 basis points on 1 October, up 13.2bp on the session, and one commentator reported that the 10-year OAT-Bund spread rose above 140 basis points over the following days. The franc-squeeze risk carried by both negative tactical factors is therefore partly underway. We keep the verdict unchanged, but we would run the tactical position at reduced size until a weekly close above the 200-week average shows the franc bid has been absorbed.

market_context.valuation_assessment: Both dossiers use the same REER-relative proxy and reach the same result. The SGD dossier puts the Singapore dollar 15.0% rich against the franc, with a fair value near 0.5676. The CHF dossier puts the franc 13.0% cheap against the Singapore dollar, with a fair value near 0.56753. At 0.64923 the pair is about 14.4% above that common proxy fair value. This is the BIS REER ratio (SGD 114.81 against CHF 99.87, August 2026), not a PPP model, and it reflects twenty years of an appreciating MAS band, a productivity premium, and a franc that has lost 2.83% in real effective terms over a year. Valuation is a structural headwind, not a tactical one. Neither central bank is leaning against the level: MAS is leaning against the pace of its own currency's appreciation, and the SNB has stopped leaning against franc strength. So the richness is policy-sanctioned and generates no mean-reversion trigger within six months. What the level does price is the carry and the band slope as they stand today. It does not price a flatter MAS band or an SNB hiking cycle, the two developments that would turn valuation into a live driver. (52-week intraday range 0.60333-0.65500, spot at the 89th percentile; the closing high of 0.65408 printed on 2026-09-30. The rally from the 2026-05-29 close of 0.61183 to that high was 422 pips, or 6.9%, in four months; September alone contributed 182 pips, +2.85%, with four straight higher closes after the SNB's 24 September hold.)

market_context.recent_regime: The pair spent June to September in a carry-driven, low-volatility grind higher. It was helped by the BoJ, Norges Bank and RBA hikes, which pushed carry funding toward the franc, and by an SNB hold on 24 September that dropped its elevated-intervention language. The grind ended abruptly on 1 October, when three franc-positive developments landed in one session. Swiss September CPI rose to 1.0%. France's 2027 budget was unveiled and the OAT-Bund spread jumped above 130bp. And the pair hit a 52-week high and reversed in a key-reversal day. The franc's move was much larger against the euro than against the Singapore dollar. One source reported that EUR/CHF fell to a two-month low around 0.9300, which is roughly 1.6% below the CHF dossier's 0.94562, while SGD/CHF fell only 0.95% from its high close and has since regained 14 pips. The narrative is now a contest between carry-plus-band appreciation and a European sovereign haven bid that this pair cannot hedge.

bilateral_carry_analysis.carry_assessment: The bilateral carry is about +192bp a year in the long-SGD direction. It uses the 6-month SGS T-bill cut-off of 1.92% (24 September auction) as the SGD short-rate proxy, because MAS sets no policy rate, against the SNB's 0.00%. On 3-month compounded SORA (1.06% average in Q2 2026) the carry would be about 106bp, an 86bp basis uncertainty that applies to every figure. Carry-to-vol (implied) is not computable because no pair IV exists. Carry-to-realised vol: 192bp / 5.11% (payload 60-day) = 0.38; the verdict's 0.39 used the base dossier's 4.90% to 2026-09-29, and on 20-day realised (4.76%) the ratio is 0.40. Either way it is the best risk-adjusted carry available to a long-SGD position in the G10+SGD set. The carry regime is working: the pair is +5.96% over a year on top of the carry, so spot has moved with the rate differential, not against it as uncovered parity would require. The regime breaks on volatility, not on rates: the 1 October session gave back about five weeks of carry in a day. The forward points are computed by covered-parity arithmetic on the policy proxy; SGD has no listed future, so there is no market funding differential, and these points omit the term premium and the cross-currency basis and should not be read as quoted forwards.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: +0.03 on both horizons. This is a high-carry pair by construction and, more importantly, the two policy regimes are structurally opposed rather than merely differently positioned: MAS runs an appreciating S$NEER band with a one-way tightening bias while the SNB sits on a 0.00% floor with no conventional easing room and a three-year conditional forecast built on no change. The rate and policy channel is doing more of the bilateral work here than the default weight allows.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Singapore has no policy rate, so the bilateral short-rate differential is read off the 6-month SGS T-bill cut-off of 1.92% (24 September auction, the highest of 2026 and up 22bp in a fortnight) against the SNB policy rate of 0.00% held on 2026-09-24 for a fifth consecutive meeting: approximately +192bp in the base currency's favour, one of only three crosses on which SGD earns positive carry at all. At the long end the gap is similar in sign and size, SGS 10-year near 2.49% against a Swiss 10-year of 0.47% on the payload's monthly August vintage (0.58% on the CHF dossier's live print), so roughly +190 to +200bp. The transmission is doubly favourable: the pair earns carry AND the base currency's policy instrument is an appreciating exchange-rate band of about 1.25% a year, so the policy regime itself delivers trade-weighted base-currency appreciation independent of yield. Against that, the market prices close to a 50% chance of an SNB hike at the 2026-12-10 assessment and at least 0.75% by September 2027, which is pricing that would have to be unwound for the carry to persist unchallenged; the Swiss front end has already added 19bp over the month on it. No SGD policy decision appears in the gated schedule and the SNB decision falls outside the tactical window, so within four weeks the differential can only hold or widen on data, not narrow on a scheduled event.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the question is whether the differential narrows, and the only scheduled event capable of narrowing it is the SNB assessment of 2026-12-10, the single decision in the gated calendar for either leg. Three outcomes matter. A hold with no tightening signal, which the SNB's own three-year conditional forecast of 0.7%/0.8%/0.8% on an unchanged rate implies and which OCBC explicitly expects, would strip roughly 75bp of embedded hikes out of the Swiss curve and widen the effective differential without MAS doing anything. A hold with a raised forecast validates the market and compresses it. A hike inverts the largest single input behind this stance. On the base side the slope does the work: a 1.25% band appreciating at about 0.6% per half-year, with a 40% probability of a steepening to 1.50% at the October review, and no easing expected before mid-2027 since MAS has said core inflation moderates only from around then. The term structure reinforces rather than contradicts: Singapore short rates are repricing upward with US yields (6M T-bill +22bp in a fortnight, 10-year SGS +54bp on the year) while Swiss 10-year funding remains below 0.6%, so the carry gap is widening at the margin rather than closing.

carry_analysis.carry_regime: Carry is working for this pair and is the pair's defining feature. The franc is the market's preferred funding leg — OCBC describes it as still a low-yield funding currency after the September SNB hold, and Reuters and Bloomberg-sourced reporting describe a rotation of carry funding out of the yen and into the franc — while the Singapore dollar is a low-volatility, policy-supported receiver of that funding. The regime breaks on a volatility event, not on a rate event, because the franc's covering flows are violent while its carry accrual is steady.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The growth differential is the widest in the G10+SGD cross-section and runs decisively in the base currency's favour: Singapore grew 5.9% year on year and 1.4% quarter on quarter in Q2 2026 against Switzerland's 2.63% and 1.885%. The Swiss quarterly figure is genuinely strong and is the reason this is a 60 rather than a 70, but SECO attributes roughly half of it to the volatile chemical-pharmaceutical sector and expects second-half moderation, while Singapore's government raised its 2026 forecast to 4.5-5.5% from 2.0-4.0% and non-oil domestic exports rose 46.2% year on year in August. The inflation differential matters more for the pair than the growth differential because it determines which central bank has a reaction function at all: MAS core at 2.2% sits in the upper half of its 1.5-2.5% range, while Swiss core at 0.40% is the lowest reading in the set. The complication, and it is new, is that Swiss September headline CPI printed 1.0% year on year on 2026-10-01 against 0.80% in August — a post-valuation datum that narrows the headline gap to Singapore's 2.3% and feeds the December SNB hike probability directly. Transmission is through relative policy: a Singapore economy running above potential with core above its midpoint keeps the band tightening-biased, while Swiss core at 0.4% keeps the SNB anchored even if headline wobbles. Pass-2 context (does not alter the score): the September print details have since become available. Swiss core CPI rose to 0.5% year on year in September from 0.4% in August, and inflation excluding petroleum products held at 0.3%, which supports the verdict's reading that the headline rise is energy-driven. The same analysis notes that the SNB's forecast path implies Q4 inflation averaging 1.2%, so a further headline rise in the October and November prints is already inside the SNB's own forecast and is not a surprise against it.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the core-inflation gap outlasts the growth gap and is what the pair ultimately trades on, because it fixes the sequencing of the two reaction functions. Swiss core at 0.40% with nominal wage growth at 0.40% gives the SNB no persistence to respond to, and both the SNB's own conditional path and SECO's panel forecast of 0.6% average inflation for 2026 and 2027 say the September headline tick is energy rather than trend. On the Singapore side, Enterprise Singapore lifted the 2026 NODX forecast to 14-16% from 3-5% and the MAS survey sees 2027 growth at 3.1%, near potential with a positive output gap, which keeps core between roughly 2.0% and 2.6% into Q1 2027 and keeps the band one-way. The symmetric risk is concentration: Singapore's surge is a single-cycle bet on hyperscaler capex and a memory-cycle turn would remove the base currency's growth and external support within two quarters, while the Swiss economy would be relatively insulated and the franc would gain on the risk-off accompanying it. That double hit is why confidence is 56 rather than 65.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: This is a haven-versus-haven pair and that is why it refuses to score. The franc is the global safe haven and the Singapore dollar is the regional one, so a generic risk-off does not produce a clean directional signal — it produces a race between two quality bids in which the franc normally wins on liquidity and the Singapore dollar wins only when the stress is specifically Asian or Chinese. The modal tape is franc-negative: VIX at 16.07, the S&P 500 up 14.33% year to date, investment-grade spreads at 83bp and gold down 6.00% over the month all deny the quote currency its bid, while Singapore's STI set a record in early September and China's PMI returned to 50.1. Against that, the live European sovereign channel is now firing rather than latent — the OAT-Bund spread was already at a one-year high of 111.2bp on 2026-09-29 and reporting dated 2026-10-05 describes French debt concerns intensifying and investors moving into the franc as a haven. The two forces are genuinely offsetting over four weeks, and the honest answer is Neutral rather than a manufactured direction. The volatility asymmetry is worth stating: both legs are low-vol in the body, so the pair's distribution is thin in the middle and fat on the downside, because a franc squeeze is violent while a Singapore dollar rally is metered by the band.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over six months the cancellation holds but the shape of the distribution becomes the point. The modal path — AI-led expansion continuing, contained energy shock, no euro-area accident — is mildly pair-positive, because it leaves the franc as the funding leg of choice and the Singapore dollar as a quality receiver. The two tails are both pair-negative and that is the asymmetry a Neutral conceals and must therefore state. A global volatility event bids the franc hard and non-linearly; the same event, if it originates in an AI-capex reversal, simultaneously removes the base currency's growth and export engine. A euro-area sovereign accident out of France routes capital into francs specifically rather than into Asian quality. The one genuinely pair-positive tail is an Iran settlement, which would be doubly franc-negative — removing the haven bid and the energy-driven inflation impulse behind SNB hike pricing at once — while cutting Singapore's import bill. Expectation-weighted, these roughly offset; skew-weighted they do not, which caps conviction on the whole pair rather than this factor alone.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Positioning is the clearest argument against this pair and it is measurable on only one of the two legs, which is itself informative. On the quote currency, CFTC leveraged funds were net short 16,457 franc contracts in the week to 2026-09-22, a fifth consecutive week of short building and, at 12.3% of open interest, the most stretched reading in the cached sample; asset managers were short a further 35,523; open interest collapsed 22.1% in a single week while the directional net extended. That is a concentrated, fragile short book, and reporting through September describes carry traders actively rotating funding from the yen into the franc, which deepens it. A combined short of that character is the raw material of a squeeze, and a franc squeeze is a fall in this pair. On the base currency there is no futures contract and therefore no comparable measure, but the S$NEER was estimated 1.68-1.9% above its band mid-point in late July and official reserves rose S$48.71bn over the year to S$550.73bn, a pattern consistent with MAS absorbing inflows rather than letting the trade-weighted currency run. So the two legs point the same way for the pair: the upside is capped by an official seller on the base side and threatened by a concentrated short on the quote side.

tactical.contrarian_case: The contrarian case against this pair is that it is a consensus carry trade wearing the clothes of a fundamental view. A trade whose both legs are crowded in the same direction does not need its thesis to be wrong to lose money; it only needs volatility.

strategic.historical_analogue: Repeated post-2022 episodes in which franc shorts were squeezed on European political events and then rebuilt within weeks at unchanged carry; the position's persistence, not its level, is the historical regularity.

A franc that weakens therefore loses its official bid rather than gaining one, which is a structural argument for the pair and against the squeeze story, provided no volatility event arrives.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: This is the rare pair in which both legs run enormous external surpluses, so the factor is about the differential rather than the level, and over four weeks that differential produces no identifiable transaction demand. Singapore's current account is projected at 16.6% of GDP for 2026 against Switzerland's 9.198% in Q2 2026 — a gap of roughly 7.4 percentage points in the base currency's favour, second and third largest in the G10+SGD set behind Norway. Direct bilateral trade is small and runs the other way: IMF DOTS puts Singapore's goods exports to Switzerland at $2.2bn against imports of $8.1bn for a net deficit of $5.8bn in 2024, a flow that is structurally quote-currency-positive but is dominated by precious metals and pharmaceuticals rather than by cyclical trade, and the mirror data disagree materially ($6.5bn/$3.9bn on the Swiss side), which is the signature of gold and bonded-vault movements rather than real activity. High-frequency signals also offset: Singapore's NODX rose 46.2% year on year in August while Switzerland's monthly trade balance narrowed to CHF 3.786bn from CHF 5.742bn, but Singapore's surplus is partly absorbed by MAS reserve accumulation rather than reaching the spot market. Neutral is the honest tactical read.

Both economies run structurally entrenched surpluses, so the question is which is larger and which is growing. net_commodity_exposure.base_commodity_profile: Singapore has no commodity export exposure; it is a net crude importer and a refining, bunkering and physical-trading hub. Per the framework's direction rules, oil up is mildly negative for SGD through the import bill, LNG/JKM up is negative, and the offset is that refining margins and trading activity rise with energy volatility. The base currency's commodity sensitivity is therefore real but second-order and partly self-hedging.
net_commodity_exposure.quote_commodity_profile: Switzerland likewise has no commodity export exposure and is a net energy importer with energy at roughly 3.5% of its CPI basket. Its genuine commodity link is gold, and it runs through shared safe-haven demand rather than trade: gold up is CHF-positive. Precious metals are nonetheless 39.9% of Swiss goods exports by value, so physical gold flows also dominate the bilateral trade line.
net_commodity_exposure.net_effect_calculation: Oil +10%: base currency mildly negative (net importer, −), quote currency mildly negative on the import bill (−) but positive on policy, because a 10% oil move feeds Swiss headline CPI and therefore the December SNB hike probability, which is the quote currency's single largest live repricing lever. Net the pair is modestly LOWER on an oil spike, because the energy channel reaches the franc through rates while it reaches the Singapore dollar only through the trade account, which MAS absorbs. Gold +10%: base currency neutral, quote currency positive (++ via the haven channel per the direction rules), so the pair falls — gold is the cleaner and larger lever of the two. Gold −10%, as realised over the past month, is pair-positive. LNG/JKM up: base currency negative (−−), quote currency negative but less so, so the pair falls modestly. Netting across all three, the pair's commodity exposure is net SHORT energy and net SHORT gold.
net_commodity_exposure.scenario_oil_up_10pct: Pair modestly lower. The import-bill hit is shared, but only the quote currency converts it into a policy repricing — a Swiss headline CPI move toward 1.2% would lift December SNB hike odds materially and bid the franc through the front end. Estimated effect is second-order relative to the carry, but directionally negative for the pair.
net_commodity_exposure.scenario_oil_down_10pct: Pair modestly higher, and this is the cleaner of the two directions. Lower crude removes the inflation impulse behind SNB hike pricing — doubly franc-negative, since it also removes the Middle East haven premium — while cutting Singapore's import bill and supporting regional growth. An Iran settlement is the version of this scenario with a date attached to it.
net_commodity_exposure.dominant_commodity_driver: Gold, not oil. Gold is the quote currency's only genuine commodity link and it is a haven link rather than a trade link, so it moves the pair directly with no offsetting base-currency exposure; the 6.00% monthly gold decline is the single most pair-positive commodity fact in this cycle. Oil is the secondary driver and reaches the pair through Swiss inflation and the SNB rather than through either trade account.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: +0.01 on both horizons. The entire bilateral thesis turns on a communication asymmetry rather than on a rate move: MAS guides to a one-way appreciating band with no easing before mid-2027, while the SNB publishes a three-year conditional forecast built on an unchanged 0% that the market declines to believe. The gap between what one central bank says and what the market prices for the other is the pair's single largest resolvable uncertainty.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Guidance diverges about as cleanly as two central banks allow. MAS tightened twice in 2026 — about +50bp of slope in April and a further 'very slight' increase on 27 July — kept its 1.5-2.5% core and headline forecast range, and said the positive output gap would widen slightly in 2026; its revealed preference is to move ahead of consensus, since only 4 of 18 analysts expected the July move. The SNB held at 0.00% for a fifth time on 2026-09-24, published a conditional forecast of 0.7%/0.8%/0.8% constructed explicitly on an unchanged rate, and — the single most pair-relevant line of the quarter — dropped June's 'increased' willingness to intervene, reverting to its standard formulation. A central bank removing an elevated-intervention flag while its currency depreciates is signalling comfort with the depreciation. OCBC reads the same September statement as toning down intervention language without a hawkish shift and judges the SNB unlikely to validate the market's hike pricing. Both credibility records are excellent, so the market does not test either framework; what it does is price an SNB hike the SNB has not guided to, and that mispricing is the pair's tactical edge. The sequencing favours the base currency: the MAS October statement, though not on the gated calendar, would fall inside or at the edge of the tactical window, well before the SNB's December assessment. MAS also observes a 21-day pre-statement quiet period, during which staff involved in formulating policy refrain from commenting on monetary policy, so there will be no MAS signalling before the decision.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Event risk is asymmetric against this pair over four weeks, and that asymmetry is the whole of the stance. The two live binaries — the French budget confrontation and the Iran sequencing talks — have payoffs that are large and franc-positive on failure and only modest and franc-negative on success, while the base currency's own event set is close to two-sided. The French channel is the sharper of the two: the OAT-Bund spread was already at a one-year high of 111.2bp on 2026-09-29 against a 74.2bp average, French debt is 119% of GDP, a EUR 54bn budget package faces a vote, and reporting dated 2026-10-05 describes capital leaving French assets for the franc as a haven. The Iran channel cuts the other way for the pair — a settlement would remove the franc's haven bid and the energy impulse behind SNB hike pricing while cutting Singapore's import bill — but the recovery of regional crude exports to just under 80% of pre-war suggests the market has already partly banked it. On the base side, the October MAS statement is a binary that skews mildly pair-positive whatever the outcome, since a hold still leaves a 1.25% appreciating band, and Singapore's domestic political risk is negligible. Netting a fat franc-positive tail against a thin, partly-priced pair-positive one gives Bearish. Read this way, the franc-positive tail has been partly realised rather than merely priced. We flag that pass 1's 58 confidence on this factor would probably be higher on today's evidence. strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over six months both binaries become genuinely two-sided and they point in opposite directions for the pair, which is a real Neutral rather than an absence of analysis. tactical.bilateral_analysis: This is the cleanest Neutral in the book and it is Neutral at high confidence because the evidence for immateriality is strong on both sides. Both sovereigns are top-rated — Singapore AAA affirmed by Fitch with a stable outlook on 2026-04-02, Switzerland AAA or Aaa from all five agencies with stable outlooks and no action in the research window — and both run balanced or surplus budgets with declining or investment-backed debt. Singapore projects an FY2026 overall surplus of S$8.5bn, 1.0% of GDP, after a revised FY2025 surplus of 1.9%, with gross debt issued to develop the bond market rather than to fund deficits and a strongly positive net asset position. Switzerland ran a zero federal balance in 2025 with general government gross debt at 39.4% of GDP falling to a projected 38.5% in 2026, held down by a constitutional debt brake. There is no rating differential, no issuance stress on either side and no fiscal event inside the window. The one way this factor could turn directional runs through a euro-area sovereign accident repricing Swiss credit quality upward relative to the region — but that transmission is already counted in Factors 3 and 7, and counting it again here would inflate the score dishonestly.

strategic.rationale: At strategic weights the structural factors take over and they all point the same way. Policy & Rates holds 0.27 and contributes +0.1728, External Balance rises from 0.06 to 0.16 and contributes +0.0896, Guidance rises to 0.13 and contributes +0.0754, and Inflation & Growth adds +0.056 — together the whole of the +0.3938, with no offsetting line anywhere in the book. The mechanism is coherent rather than coincidental: Singapore's 16.6%-of-GDP current account surplus funds the reserves that make the band credible, the band converts above-midpoint core inflation into a mechanical 0.6% of trade-weighted appreciation per half-year, and MAS's guidance rules out easing before mid-2027; on the other side the SNB has published a three-year conditional forecast that keeps inflation inside its band on an unchanged 0.00% rate, OCBC expects no move well into 2027, and the bank dropped its elevated-intervention language while its currency fell. This cross is the one expression in which the base currency's constraint (negative carry to high-yielders) does not bind and the quote currency's support (its surplus) is outweighed by a larger surplus on the other side. What is priced is the 192bp differential; what is not priced is the band slope, the probability that roughly 75bp of SNB tightening is removed on 2026-12-10, or the 7.4-point current-account differential. The path of least resistance is a slow staircase in the pair's favour at roughly the pace of the band, accelerating only if the SNB confirms its own forecast in December. The dated catalysts are the SNB assessment of 2026-12-10 — the only decision in the gated file for either leg — the MAS October and January statements, neither of which appears in the gated schedule, and the turn-of-year dollar funding window that clusters with the SNB date. A clean number with an unscored tail deserves the same conviction as a messier number with a scored one.

The only published pair numbers come from model-driven retail pages. For example, BestExchangeRates' mid-September note carried a mild downside near-term bias with an expected range of 0.6340-0.6450, a range spot has already broken above. Such extrapolations are not consensus, and we do not measure ourselves against them. The research that does exist is at the leg level, and it is split on the decisive question of the SNB. On the dovish side, OCBC wrote after the September hold that the SNB is unlikely to validate the market's relatively hawkish pricing, with rates unchanged well into 2027 even as OIS prices a meaningful December hike probability, and UBS judges the inflation rise modest and unlikely to force the SNB to raise rates in 2026. On the base leg, the October MAS statement is closer to consensus: CIMB forecasts a third consecutive tightening in October, and 45% of the MAS survey agree. Research on the funding role supports the pair: Rabobank raised its 9-12 month EUR/CHF forecast to 0.95 from 0.94, while warning that the franc's safe-haven status means it could surge sharply if market anxiety rises. Our view sides with OCBC and UBS against the curve and draws the pair-bullish conclusion explained in Factors 1 and 6. Where this report's narrative departs from the scored verdict: we leave the stances unchanged, but we flag two pieces of non-price evidence that arrived after pass 1 scored. First, French stress escalated from the 111.2bp the verdict used to 130bp or more; one report noted the French-German 10-year spread briefly widened beyond 150 basis points, its highest since November 2011, which on its own breaches the CHF dossier's 140bp invalidator. Second, the MAS statement is dated no later than 14 October rather than late October. The first development argues for higher confidence on the Bearish tactical Factor 7. The second brings a pair-positive binary forward into the tactical window. Their net effect on the score is ambiguous, and our response is to size down, not to re-score.
consensus_divergence.payoff_if_right: If the SNB merely confirms its forecast, roughly 75bp of tightening comes out of the Swiss front end, producing 0.6640 by end-Q1 2027, about 209 pips above the indicative carry-implied six-month forward.
consensus_divergence.risk_if_wrong: The risk is concentrated in one afternoon: an SNB hike on 2026-12-10 would take the pair to the 0.6300 downside case.

cross_horizon_consistency.explanation: Both horizons are Bullish and the strategic reading is the stronger of the two, which is unusual and worth explaining. The direction is identical because the same three forces drive it at both horizons: a 192bp carry, an appreciating band against a zero floor, and a central bank communication gap that resolves in the pair's favour if the SNB simply does what it has published. The strength differs because the two negative tactical lines — Flows at -0.058 and Event Risk at -0.029 — both decay to zero over six months. The franc short is its structural resting state as a funding currency and rebuilds at carry rather than mean-reverting, and the dated French catalyst either resolves or is absorbed. Meanwhile External Balance rises from a 0.06 weight to 0.16 and turns from Neutral to Bullish as the 7.4-point current-account differential starts to matter. Four factors change stance across the horizons: Flows from Bearish to Neutral, Event Risk from Bearish to Neutral, External Balance from Neutral to Bullish, and USD Liquidity from Bullish to Neutral.
cross_horizon_consistency.trading_implication: Same direction at both horizons, so there is no inflection to navigate — but the composition difference matters for how the position is carried. The tactical score is lower because it correctly prices a dated, firing franc-positive catalyst; the strategic score is higher because that catalyst has decayed out of it, not because the fundamentals improve. A position built on the strategic case should therefore expect the tactical window to be its most dangerous stretch, and the correlated cluster of 2026-12-10 and the year-end funding turn is the second. The absence of any option market on the cross means the tail cannot be hedged within the pair, only proxied through EUR/CHF or USD/CHF at basis risk, which is an argument for smaller size rather than for a different direction. Pass-2 note: in practice the strategic position should be built inside the tactical window but scaled in (see the strategic execution plan). The MAS statement is due by 14 October and the 200-week resolution is due within the same fortnight, so both early confirmations fall at the point of greatest tactical risk.

catalysts.rationale: Headline CPI rose 1.0% year on year from 0.8%, in line with consensus, and core edged up to 0.5%. The print sustains roughly even odds of a December SNB hike and keeps the Swiss 2-year near 0.31%, narrowing the pair's carry advantage in expectation. Because ex-petroleum inflation held at 0.3%, the move does not show the domestic persistence that would justify a cycle.

The budget launch pushed the French spread to a crisis-era level, and capital outflows from French assets are supporting the franc. The pair's key-reversal session that day is the price signature of this catalyst. The Singapore dollar has no offsetting exposure, so the transmission to the pair is one-sided.

catalysts.event: SNB and MAS official foreign reserves (September data)
catalysts.rationale: MAS lists official foreign reserves data for September on 07 Oct 2026. A rise of S$1-5bn would confirm MAS is still absorbing appreciation pressure near the top of its band, which caps the base leg tactically. A large fall in SNB reserves or sight deposits would signal franc buying, which no source currently expects.

catalysts.event: MAS Monetary Policy Statement and Macroeconomic Review (no later than 14 October); Q3 advance GDP
catalysts.rationale: MAS's advance release calendar sets the October 2026 statement for no later than 14 October, with the Macroeconomic Review the same day, and the FOMC meets later, on October 27-28. That brings the pair's main base-leg binary forward into the tactical window. A steepening to about 1.50% (our probability 40%) adds 30-60 pips on the day, while a hold leaves a 1.25% appreciating band working against a franc pinned at zero. The Q3 advance GDP estimate is normally released the same morning.

catalysts.event: French parliamentary budget process and possible no-confidence motions (week 3 of October into November 2026)
catalysts.rationale: The €54bn savings package faces a fragmented assembly, and the political test is framed as running into November. A government collapse would push the spread towards or past the 145-150bp local highs ING cites and force covering in a franc short at 12.3% of open interest. A credible pass would narrow the spread and release the carry bid.

catalysts.event: Singapore September NODX (Enterprise Singapore, week of 19 October)
catalysts.rationale: August NODX rose 46.2% year on year, and this series carries both the growth differential and the current-account differential in the pair's strategic case. A print of 20% or more confirms the AI cycle. One below 15% would be the first crack in the strategic Bullish.

catalysts.event: Singapore September CPI and MAS core inflation
catalysts.rationale: MAS lists Consumer Price Developments for 23 October, after the policy statement. Core at 2.3% or more would widen the core gap with Switzerland (0.5%) beyond 180bp and validate any October steepening. A drop to 2.0% or below would argue the band has peaked.

Tight-but-orderly dollars lift Singapore short rates and deepen the franc's funding role, widening the pair's differential from both ends (Factor 10 tactical); impact is mild. Sources disagree on October hike odds: the CHF dossier cites about 47% on CME FedWatch, while another report put the October hike probability at about 70%. A disorderly hawkish surprise that lifts VIX would reverse the sign through the haven race.

The ECB matters for this pair through EUR/CHF. A hawkish ECB amid French stress widens intra-euro spreads, which is franc-positive. A dovish hold that relieves OAT pressure is franc-negative, so the decision moves the pair only through the French channel.

The calendar shows the October inflation release on 2026-11-03. The SNB's own path needs Q4 to average about 1.2%, so a print of 1.1-1.3% would be in line with the forecast, not hawkish. A print of 1.4% or more, or core at 0.9% or more, would validate December hike pricing and is the most pair-negative realistic data outcome before the SNB.

catalysts.event: SNB quarterly monetary policy assessment (only scheduled decision for either leg in the gated calendar)
catalysts.rationale: This is the pair's pivotal binary. A hold with a conditional forecast still inside the band on an unchanged rate removes roughly 75bp of embedded tightening and widens the effective differential. A hike or a normalisation reference inverts Factors 1 and 6 together and targets the 0.6300 strategic downside case.

catalysts.event: Year-end US dollar funding window (late December 2026, week 4)
catalysts.rationale: Turn-of-year balance-sheet constraints historically squeeze funding currencies higher; the impact is asymmetric against the franc short. The franc is the most exposed funding leg in G10, while MAS's S$550.73bn of reserves insulate the base leg. The window falls in the same fortnight as the SNB assessment.

catalysts.event: MAS Monetary Policy Statement (January 2027, week 4; date inferred from quarterly cadence)
catalysts.rationale: Nearly all survey respondents expect no change. A hold at a 1.25-1.50% slope confirms the appreciation path that carries the strategic case into Q1 2027. The date is week-level, inferred from MAS's quarterly cadence.

invalidators.mechanism: The AI cycle drives both the growth differential and the current-account differential, and its reversal would coincide with a franc-bidding risk-off.
